title: Sweet Chestnut: Ancient Chestnuts You Can Visit
meta_description: The chestnut whose bark spirals with age. The Hundred-Horse Chestnut on Etna, one tree on three stems, is put at about 2,200 years.
intro: On the slope of Etna above Sant'Alfio, what looks like three enormous chestnuts is one tree: the Hundred-Horse Chestnut, named for a queen said to have sheltered under it with a hundred mounted knights, and put at about 2,200 years by Italy's agricultural research council in 2022. Sweet chestnut collects stories because it stays around long enough. Corsica's Bread Tree at Pianello is so called because for centuries its nuts were the bread. In January 1949 a runaway bus above Trento was stopped by a chestnut, and local accounts still argue about which one. The trunk gives the age away better than any plaque, because as a chestnut ages its bark starts to spiral around the stem, and on the oldest the whole trunk looks wrung out like a towel. Charles II is behind the Greenwich Park tree, planted for the formal avenues he ordered after 1660.
